National Parliament
National Assembly
Twenty-first Session
Complete Minutes of Proceedings
Ashoj 2083
16 Friday
Meeting No. - 42
The meeting of the National Assembly commenced today at 13:20 hrs under the chairmanship of the Right Honourable Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal, Chairperson.
Right Honourable Chairperson: - Honourable members, the meeting of the National Assembly commences today. Honourable members, I will provide time to the Honourable members who have registered their names to speak during the Zero Hour. First, Honourable Member Goma Devi Timalsina.
Honourable Member Goma Devi Timalsina (Nepali Communist Party): - (13:20 hrs) Chairperson, the incident at Bhote Koshi has devastated the area and many containers carrying goods have been washed away. There has been significant loss of life and property. The surviving containers are stuck at the Necud customs via the Korala border in Mustang. Due to the lack of a proper road to bring all those commercial goods, the goods have not been able to arrive. I wish to draw the attention of the government through the Right Honourable Chairperson to take steps to make the road suitable for bringing those goods and to provide some relief to the traders between Dashain and Tihar. Thank you.
Honourable Member Jagat Bahadur Pariyar.
Right Honourable Chairperson: - (13:21 hrs) Honourable Member Jagat Bahadur Pariyar (Nepali Communist Party): - (13:22 hrs) Chairperson, due to continuous rainfall across the country for some time, there has been significant loss of life and property. Similarly, the Dodhara Chandani bridge over the Mahakali River in Kanchanpur district has been damaged. Due to the damage to this suspension bridge, approximately 50,000 people residing in Dodhara Chandani are affected in their movement to and from the district headquarters. I wish to request through the Right Honourable Chairperson that the damaged Dodhara Chandani bridge be immediately repaired and reconstructed so that the affected people can travel easily. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: - Honourable Member Nar Bahadur Bisht.
(13:22 hrs) Honourable Member Nar Bahadur Bisht (Nepali Communist Party): - (13:23 hrs) Chairperson, the Baijchaur-Khambagade road has been in limbo for more than 7 years. The contractor has not done any work yet. Dashain and Tihar have arrived. I want to tell the federal government that road networks across the country are blocked. What is being done for the repair work to facilitate the public's travel during Dashain and Tihar? I wish to draw the attention of the government through the Chairperson. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: - Honourable Member Bhuvan Bahadur Sunar.
(13:23 hrs) Honourable Member Bhuvan Bahadur Sunar (Nepali Communist Party): - (13:23 hrs) Chairperson, there is good within the bad and bad within the good. The list of surnames of the Dalit community, compiled with great effort by the National Dalit Commission, has been approved by the cabinet through the efforts of Minister Sita Kumari Pariyar. I extend my heartfelt congratulations to the Minister. I expect the Dalit Rights and Development Act to be enacted soon. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: - Honourable Member Madan Kumari Shah "Garima".
(13:24 hrs) Honourable Member Madan Kumari Shah "Garima" (Nepali Communist Party): - (13:24 hrs) Chairperson, the 29th session is concluding today. During this period, the Honourable Prime Minister made a statement in the House of Representatives that Nepal has encroached upon Indian territory, which is an anti-national and anti-sovereignty statement. This statement by the Prime Minister is one hundred percent false. His statement has tarnished the country's reputation and international image, and has deeply hurt national pride, national interest, and the sentiments of the Nepali people. His statement in diplomatic discourse has put us on the defensive. Therefore, I strongly demand through the Right Honourable Chairperson that the Honourable Prime Minister correct his anti-national interest statement and withdraw it. Furthermore, I humbly request the Honourable Speaker through the Right Honourable Chairperson to remove the Prime Minister's statement from the parliamentary record. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: - Honourable Member Yuvraj Sharma.
(13:25 hrs) Honourable Member Yuvraj Sharma (Nepali Congress): - (13:24 hrs) Chairperson, today is the death anniversary of my father, and I wish to remember him first. He was both my hero and my source of inspiration. Although I was known by his name in my youth, my own identity began to form after I entered the field of work, which was perhaps a natural transition. Right Honourable Chairperson, Nepal presented its problems from the platform of the United Nations, which is becoming weaker; it was necessary to do so. Thank you. However, the roar of the Magar and the visit of the President of friendly nation China to America overshadowed all these scenes. Right Honourable Chairperson, after that, we were like watching the realistic scene of the Mahabharata war with severed heads. When voices are heard from our neighbors saying that climate change has not happened, but rather we have changed, then it is automatically proven that even poison that is not consumed can be harmful. Finally, today, October 2nd, I bid farewell remembering the extraordinary Mahatma Gandhi. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: - Honourable Member Rajendra Laxmi Gaire.
(13:26 hrs) Honourable Member Rajendra Laxmi Gaire (Nepali Communist Party): - (13:26 hrs) Chairperson, a great calamity has befallen Nepal for about a month. Especially the floods from the 8th to the 11th have washed away the Kaligandaki corridor, from the Keladi bridge to the bridge connecting Hamichaur-Mirmi-Gullmi. What has the government planned for the passengers crossing back and forth during this Dashain? What arrangements are being made? I wish to draw the government's attention. Another issue is that due to these floods, the paddy crops of many farmers have been destroyed. What is the compensation package the government will provide to the farmers? I wish to draw the government's attention to this as well. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: - Honourable Member Suresh Kumar Alemagar.
(13:27 hrs) Honourable Member Suresh Kumar Alemagar (Nepali Communist Party): - (13:27 hrs) Chairperson, the agenda of our National Assembly includes the Nepal Sambat every day. Nepal Sambat 1146. This Sambat also has months and dates. I request that this be written. For example, today is the month of Yala and the date is Khasta. I request that it be written as Nepal Sambat 1146 Yala or Yalaga Khasta. Not just the Sambat. This started during the tenure of Honourable Prime Minister Prachanda. Let this be completed, just as we write about Vikram Sambat. Similarly, due to natural disasters, various roads are closed. As the festivals celebrated by Nepalis are approaching, I wish to state that the government should work on an express basis to open these roads and that the public should overcome this state of helplessness. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: - Honourable members, the order of speaking during the Zero Hour concludes here.
Right Honourable Chairperson: - Honourable members, now the Question and Answer session will commence as per Chapter 8 of the National Assembly Rules, 2075. Honourable members, I will now provide time for the Honourable Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle to table the answer to the oral question related to the Ministry of Finance, asked by Honourable Member Jagat Timilsina, to the Honourable Home Minister Sudhan Gurung in the assembly.
Honourable Home Minister Mr. Sudhan Gurung: - (13:29 hrs) Chairperson, with the permission of the Chairperson, I am tabling the answer to the oral question related to the Ministry of Finance, asked by Honourable Member Jagat Timilsina, in the assembly. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: - (13:29 hrs) Honourable members, I will now provide time for the Honourable Home Minister Sudhan Gurung to table the answers to the oral questions related to the Ministry of Home Affairs, asked by Honourable Member Padam Bahadur Pariyar, Honourable Member Bishnukumari Sapkota, and Honourable Member Shree Krishna Prasad Adhikari, in the assembly.
Honourable Home Minister Mr. Sudhan Gurung: - (13:30 hrs) Chairperson, with the permission of the Chairperson, I am tabling the answers to the oral questions related to the Ministry of Home Affairs, asked by Honourable Member Padam Bahadur Pariyar, Honourable Member Bishnukumari Sapkota, and Honourable Member Shree Krishna Prasad Adhikari, in the assembly. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: - (13:30 hrs) Honourable members, I will now provide time for the Honourable Home Minister Sudhan Gurung to table the answers to the oral questions asked by Honourable Member Madan Kumari Shah "Garima" and Honourable Member Padam Bahadur Pariyar, related to the Ministry of Physical Infrastructure and Transport, and the answer to the written question asked by Honourable Member Somnath Poudel.
Honourable Home Minister Mr. Sudhan Gurung: - (13:31 hrs) Chairperson, with the permission of the Chairperson, I am tabling the answers to the oral questions asked by Honourable Member Madan Kumari Shah "Garima" and Honourable Member Padam Bahadur Pariyar, related to the Ministry of Physical Infrastructure and Transport, and the answer to the written question asked by Honourable Somnath Poudel, in the assembly. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: - (13:31 hrs) Honourable members, I inform you that the copies of the tabled written and oral questions' answers have been placed in the pigeonholes. Honourable members, I will now provide time for the Honourable Minister of Land Management, Cooperatives, and Poverty Alleviation, Honourable Pratibha Rawal, on behalf of the Honourable Prime Minister, to present the 63rd Annual Report of the Auditor General 2083, the Annual Report of the Election Commission Nepal for the fiscal year 2081/082, and the Annual Report of the Muslim Commission Nepal for the fiscal year 2081/082.
Honourable Minister of Land Management, Cooperatives, and Poverty Alleviation Ms. Pratibha Rawal: - (13:32 hrs) Chairperson, with the permission of the Chairperson, I present the 63rd Annual Report of the Auditor General 2083, the Annual Report of the Election Commission Nepal for the fiscal year 2081/082, and the Annual Report of the Muslim Commission Nepal for the fiscal year 2081/082 to this Honourable Assembly. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: - (13:32 hrs) Honourable members, I will now provide time for the Honourable Chairperson of the Legislation Management Committee, Krishna Bahadur Rokaya, to present the Annual Report of the Legislation Management Committee for the fiscal year 2082/083 to the assembly.
Honourable Chairperson of the Legislation Management Committee Mr. Krishna Bahadur Rokaya: - (13:33 hrs) Chairperson, the work areas of the Legislation Management Committee, one of the four thematic committees of the Federal Parliament National Assembly, include discussing bills received from the assembly as per Rule 147 of the National Assembly Rules, 2075, managing bills, monitoring and researching the implementation of laws, and legislative interrelations between federal units. The committee has been continuously working in all three areas. Bills received by the committee are discussed based on the date of receipt, and considering the constitutional and legal limits for bills to remain in the committee, priority is given to bills under consideration, bills received from the House of Representatives, and financial bills, taking into account the Honourable Minister's schedule for discussions on bills. Only one committee under the National Assembly...

The meeting will discuss the bill, and amendments have been made to allow amendment proponents, experts, and stakeholders to participate in the theoretical discussion, discussions with experts and stakeholders, and in some cases, discussions on the report, providing an opportunity to participate in the law-making process of the bill. Considering the time limit, experts and stakeholders have been invited to discuss the bill. In some cases, two meetings have been held on the same day, with theoretical discussions and discussions with experts and stakeholders. Similarly, suggestions from experts and stakeholders are discussed in the committee. Honorable Chairperson, a total of 89 meetings of the committee have been held during this period. Out of these, 12 bills passed by the committee have been discussed in 77 meetings and presented to the assembly. Two meetings were focused on measuring the implementation of laws, and 10 meetings were focused on other committee-related issues. In this fiscal year, the 12 bills received by the committee from the assembly were unanimously passed after committee discussions. These bills include the Water Resources Bill 2081, the Nepal Citizenship (Second Amendment) Bill 2081, the National Forensic Science Laboratory Establishment and Operation Bill 2081, the Federal Civil Service Bill 2080, the Tourism Bill 2081, the Film Bill 2081, and the Social Heritage Conservation Bill 2081. Similarly, the four ordinance replacement bills received from the House of Representatives with a message on June 9, 2083, the Bill to Amend Some Nepal Acts Related to Health Science Institutions 2083, the Property Purification and Money Laundering Prevention (Second Amendment) Bill 2083, the Public Procurement Second Amendment Bill 2083, and the Cooperative First Amendment Bill 2083 were passed with amendments by the committee on June 17, 2083, and the replacement bills were authenticated by the President after completing all procedures on the same day. Of the above bills, the Social Heritage Bill 2081 was withdrawn by the Government of Nepal on January 20, 2082. Honorable Chairperson, the agenda of other committee meetings included the farewell of honorable members whose terms in the National Assembly had expired, the welcome of newly arrived honorable members, the committee's annual report, the committee's future work plan, and the election of the chairperson. The committee meeting was also held in the presence of the Honorable Vice-Chairperson, and guidance was received. Similarly, the Common Policy and Program Committee and the Legislation Management Committee held a joint meeting by inviting the Minister and Secretary of Law, Justice, and Parliamentary Affairs. The committee has also prepared and passed the annual work plan for the upcoming fiscal year 2083/084 to further refine its work and make it more effective. In addition, to study the implementation of child participation provisions in various sections of the Children Act 2075, the committee visited five provinces, held direct discussions with some children in juvenile correction homes and child protection centers, and held discussions with local levels and ministries at the provincial level, and submitted a report to the assembly. Similarly, the committee held separate interactions regarding the law-making process of local levels with the Legislation and Provincial Affairs Committee of the Sudurpashchim Provincial Assembly and three local levels, and with the Bagmati Province Assembly and two local levels. Honorable Chairperson, I would like to inform the respected assembly that the committee has passed the report prepared by the committee, which includes the committee's activities, the status of bills, member attendance, decisions, and committee reports related to bills from July 17, 2082, to June 30, 2083, on today's meeting of October 2, 2083. Finally, I express my heartfelt gratitude to the Honorable Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, and Vice-Chairperson for their valuable suggestions, guidance, guardianship, and encouragement in making the committee's work, discussions, monitoring, and interactions effective. I also express my gratitude and thanks to the Honorable Ministers of the Government of Nepal, former chairpersons and members of the committee, honorable members of the committee, amendment proponents, and all honorable members who proposed amendments for participating and cooperating in the committee's work and the clause-by-clause discussion of the bills. I also extend thanks to the Secretary General of the Federal Parliament, the Secretary of the National Assembly, the secretaries of the secretariat, former secretary of the National Assembly, officials, secretaries, and committee secretaries of the Ministry of Law, Justice, and Parliamentary Affairs and other relevant ministries and bodies, and the staff at the committee secretariat, as well as experts, civil servants, security personnel, stakeholders, and media personnel who have provided significant direct and indirect support to the committee's work, and I expect continued cooperation in the future. Honorable Chairperson, I present the annual report of the Legislation Management Committee for the fiscal year 2082/083, passed by the committee on October 2, 2083, to this respected assembly in accordance with the provisions of Rule 159 (4) of the National Assembly Rules, 2075. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, I now provide time to the Honorable Minister of Science, Technology, and Innovation, Mahabir Pun, to present the proposal to discuss the amendments made by the House of Representatives to the National Forensic Science Laboratory Establishment and Operation Bill, 2081, which was returned with amendments from the House of Representatives. Honorable Minister of Science, Technology, and Innovation, Mr. Mahabir Pun - Honorable Chairperson, with the permission of the Chairperson, I present to this respected assembly the proposal to discuss the amendments made by the House of Representatives to the National Forensic Science Laboratory Establishment and Operation Bill, 2081, which was returned with amendments from the House of Representatives. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, the discussion on the proposal to discuss the amendments made by the House of Representatives to the National Forensic Science Laboratory Establishment and Operation Bill, 2081, presented by the Honorable Minister of Science, Technology, and Innovation, Mahabir Pun, begins. I would like to inform you that the discussion can be held on the amendments made by the House of Representatives to the bill and the related subsidiary clauses. I request the honorable members who wish to participate in the discussion and speak to provide their names within two minutes. I have set a time limit of three minutes for each honorable member participating in the discussion. Honorable Member Krishna Bahadur Rokaya. Honorable Mr. Krishna Bahadur Rokaya (Nepali Congress): Honorable Chairperson, the National Forensic Science Laboratory Establishment and Operation Bill, 2081, is a bill that originated in the National Assembly, and it was necessary to introduce this bill, and it was introduced by the then government. After this bill was submitted to the National Assembly, it was sent to the Legislation Management Committee with amendments from the honorable members after theoretical discussions, and extensive discussions were held in the Legislation Management Committee. During the discussions, many issues were raised, and specifically, this bill aims to establish and operate the National Forensic Science Laboratory to assist in the investigation of crimes and the administration of justice through the use of scientific methods and techniques for the collection, analysis, and testing of evidence, and to make the study, research, and testing of forensic science effective, reliable, and specialized. This bill had 33 clauses, and in those 33 clauses, the honorable members had proposed amendments to many clauses, and since discussions were not held there, we amended 21 clauses in the Legislation Management Committee, passed it from here, and sent it to the House of Representatives after unanimously passing it. Today, during discussions in the House of Representatives, discussions were held on some clauses, and this bill has returned to the National Assembly today with further amendments to the clauses that we had sent with amendments. Upon examination, the clauses that we had amended have been refined and further enriched. Therefore, I request that this bill be approved by the National Assembly with consensus. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Suresh Kumar Ale Magar. Honorable Mr. Suresh Kumar Ale Magar (Communist Party of Nepal): Honorable Chairperson, we are discussing the report on the National Forensic Science Laboratory Establishment and Operation Bill, 2081. First of all, as the former honorable member mentioned, this bill originated in the National Assembly, and after considerable discussion there, we moved forward with many proposals and amendments, and finally, we moved forward with consensus. This bill was further discussed in the House of Representatives, and discussions on amendments also took place. Thus, I also feel that this bill has become more refined and improved. For example, the amendment states 'in all provinces' instead of 'in provinces as needed' for the establishment of the laboratory units at the provincial level. This amendment seems to have embraced the spirit of federalism. Because, according to this amendment, branches or units of this laboratory will be established in all provinces, not just as needed. These are the issues, so I believe this bill should be moved forward. Firstly, there was a state of lawlessness regarding the establishment of the National Forensic Science Laboratory, and stakeholders were urging for such a bill and were strongly advocating for it. Accordingly, the previous government realized this fact and introduced this bill. This bill, which came in 2081, is now 2083. Firstly, the enactment of such a law was delayed from the beginning. Even counting from the time the enactment of this law began, it has been significantly delayed. This bill, which came in 2081, has reached 2083. Therefore, I believe this bill must be moved forward, and there should be no further delay in passing this bill. Therefore, I want to express my opinion that this bill, although it may not be perfect and may have some shortcomings or require amendments, these will be addressed in the future, and this bill, the National Forensic Science Laboratory Establishment and Operation Bill, 2081, should be approved by this respected National Assembly. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Sonam Geljen Sherpa. Honorable Mr. Sonam Geljen Sherpa (Nepal Communist Party, UML): Honorable Chairperson, the National Forensic Science Laboratory Establishment and Operation Bill, 2081, originated in the National Assembly, and after discussions in the National Assembly and discussions by the Legislation Committee, it was passed and sent to the House of Representatives. The House of Representatives...

Regarding that, it has been sent to the National Assembly for consensus after making some amendments. This is very important in the context of Nepal, and it has established a credible basis for Nepal's criminal investigation and other investigations in international forums. Regarding this, some suggestions have come from the House of Representatives on this technical matter, and we must consider them. I have already drawn the attention of the House regarding some technical matters that have come up. We discussed this extensively, and after this discussion, it seems the House of Representatives has also discussed it well, and it has taken a refined form. Now, regarding DNA testing, its security, and many other things, we cannot include them in the act. In this regard, I specially request the concerned minister to clarify what the security of DNA is and to include it in the procedures and regulations. What are the international practices? This matter of DNA is very important. We think of it as a small thing, but it is very important. It is a matter of one's freedom, and it is also a matter of privacy. Some things have been mentioned here, and regarding how to secure DNA, after someone's DNA is tested, the record, from criminal investigation to being acquitted by the court, can be removed. This is an important aspect of the legislation, and I welcome it. In some cases, various judgments of the Supreme Court have also raised questions about the reliability of DNA. Now that the law has been enacted, I believe that DNA will gain legal recognition effectively. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, the discussion on the amendments made by the House of Representatives to the National Forensic Science Laboratory Establishment and Operation Bill, 2085 BS, which has returned with amendments from the House of Representatives (13:49 PM), will take place in this session. Honorable members, I now provide time to the Honorable Minister of Science, Technology, and Innovation, Mahabir Pun, to respond to the issues raised in the discussion. Honorable Minister of Science, Technology, and Innovation, Mr. Mahabir Pun - (13:50 PM) - Chairperson Sir, Honorable members, regarding the bill that came today for the establishment and operation of the National Forensic Science Laboratory, first of all, it took about 20 meetings, or how many, to pass this bill in our committee, and every word, let alone the line, was a subject of intense discussion. Because this is something that has never been done before, right? We have also gained new experiences, and it took 3 months. The suggestions you sent from the National Assembly took about 3 months in the committee, and a lot of discussion has been done as much as possible. Even after such discussions, this act itself cannot be said to be complete. Therefore, there will be a need to amend the act from time to time, and this is something that will be done in the future. The matter here is that it started from a mandate. It started from NAS, not from a mandate. A laboratory was established in NAS, and then it was decided that a forensic science laboratory was needed, and it was established by mandate. And until now, work has been carried out on that basis. The Nepal Police also had a laboratory there, and the forensic science laboratory was operating in an old building within the NAS premises. What the situation was like became clear after the recent Bhotekoshi flood. We realized what condition it was operating in and what its capacity was. Because when the Bhotekoshi flood occurred, thousands of people went missing, and their bodies' DNA was to be collected and tested, and the DNA of the relatives of those missing people was to be tested. It turned out that we had nothing to test DNA. If we had to test DNA with our own known capacity, it would have taken more than a year. Even though the public has demanded immediate results, fortunately, a team of 15 people with modern equipment from the Chinese government and a team of 19 people with equipment from the Indian government came and tested at the Nepal Police laboratory, NAS laboratory, and forensic science laboratory. Only then did we realize what our capacity was. DNA testing was done at NAS, but it was mainly for researchers to test the DNA of plants and animals. They were not testing human DNA. However, the team from China was kept at NAS and the testing was done. Anyway, arrangements were made for proper DNA testing, and they also got an opportunity to learn. I would say that the condition of our laboratory is like a shed, as many of you know, or perhaps some of you know, Mahabir Pun, who established the National Innovation Center in a shed for research and invention. Our laboratory also seems to be like that shed, in terms of its capacity. That was the situation. Therefore, it is good that the act has now been passed. The law has been made on paper, but now we need to build state-of-the-art laboratories accordingly to make it work. The first laboratory is the NAS laboratory here in Kathmandu. Now, there is one laboratory in each of the remaining four provinces. They are small laboratories, also in rented houses, not on their own land. The reason for not having land in their own name is that since this institution was established by mandate, it could not acquire land for possession. Now that the act has been passed, the forensic science laboratory will be able to acquire land in its name and build laboratories. We have already made plans to build good laboratories. The situation here is that this laboratory has been nominal so far, as the government, the Ministry of Finance, has not allocated any budget. A small budget is allocated. For example, when testing DNA now, equipment worth 40 million, 40 million, 100 million rupees was brought. If such an amount is never allocated, how can that laboratory, the forensic science laboratory, or the Nepal Police laboratory become modern? No budget is allocated. Looking at the current situation, in the budget presented on Jestha 15th, a total budget of 980 million rupees has been allocated for the operation of the forensic science laboratory. Most of it is for the salaries and allowances of the technicians and staff there. And for the equipment needed there, only a small amount, not even 100 million rupees, has been allocated. Therefore, what we have done now is that the act has been passed. The act for the Ministry of Science, Technology, and Innovation has not been passed yet, but from the fund that has gone into the fund, I have already said that a list has been made. It may not be possible to modernize the forensic science laboratory in a single year. This year, we need to buy essential equipment, and what needs to be bought next year, a list is being prepared, not just here but in other provinces as well. And in doing so, they have requested a budget of 200 million rupees to purchase equipment worth 200 million rupees, and we will provide that budget. With 200 million rupees, we will buy as much equipment as possible. That's about the equipment. Modern equipment is essential for forensic science. Justice, which is ultimately delivered through research in ordinary laboratories in an ordinary way, will be an injustice to the recipient if the testing is not done properly. Therefore, 200 million rupees have been allocated for equipment, not for buildings. There is no building here in Kathmandu, no land, and no building. Now, the plan is to acquire land within the NAS premises because NAS has a large area. By acquiring land from NAS and taking possession, a large building will be constructed. For the design of this building, I have asked the DG of the Department of Building, and they are designing the building. It will cost at least 60-70 million rupees to build that building. In this way, with the budget of this year, by spending about 250-260 million rupees, not just there, but now it will be spent only there. We also need to modernize the four laboratories in other provinces and add three more. Therefore, this work is progressing. I want to inform you about this. Regarding the technical issue raised by the honorable member, there has been extensive discussion about DNA security. In fact, for about 4-5 days, only the discussion was about DNA security in the committee. It is essential to keep it very secure because it is a very sensitive matter. Its data, called the DNA data bank, should be like a bank where money is kept; similarly, there should be a bank for DNA, and how to make that bank digitally secure is a technical matter. This technical matter can be kept secure. Another thing is that I have heard that there are some rumors going around. I haven't heard it with my own ears, but I have heard from others that the DNA data is being shared with foreigners, and foreigners are also getting access to it. I heard such rumors. Specifically, it is not about sharing the DNA data of Nepalis with foreigners or leaking it. Especially, if foreigners are involved in an accident like the recent Bhotekoshi flood, about 400 or more foreigners from various countries, including Chinese, Indians, and Americans, have been affected. The DNA of those foreign citizens will be here, and according to some law or regulation, it is written in this act that it will be provided to them. It will be provided according to the prevailing rules, foreign DNA. Now, from Nepal. If our citizens go abroad and go missing or disappear in some country, we will also have to request their DNA data. It's not that we only provide it. Therefore, regarding the DNA data, we also have to request their data. The provision is made to provide the data of foreign citizens to them and to request the data of our citizens who have gone missing abroad. This will be very secure. Of course, if any data is kept in a digital format, whether in Nepal or anywhere in the world, nothing can be 100% secure. For example, even data kept by large companies like Microsoft and Amazon, however securely, is sometimes leaked by hackers.

It is heard that it has been done, it is happening, but as technology gets stronger, it will become safer. Therefore, the law has been made, and now we have to use it as best as possible. I had said that whatever is needed, not expensive things, but I have said to buy expensive things. What happens here is that when the government tenders, it tenders for the lowest value, the minimum value. But not cheap, expensive, very good. Because the equipment used in the lab for this cannot be made in Nepal, nor can it be made. Therefore, I have told everyone to buy good ones, and it will come. And what the honorable members have said is essentially this. Regarding the process of acquiring land, I have already given instructions to the secretaries regarding where and whose land to acquire. They have already started the process of who needs to submit an application for land in the relevant places. Thank you. I think these things need to be considered. Finally, I wish to extend my heartfelt greetings and best wishes to everyone for the upcoming great Nepali festivals of Dashain, Tihar, and Chhath. Our country is currently in a very difficult situation. Citizens from all 77 districts have suffered greatly due to the Bhote Koshi flood and the continuous rainfall from October 8th to 19th. Therefore, I wish everyone a happy celebration, without extravagance, in a way that upholds our customs and culture. I wish everyone a happy celebration, continuing traditions according to their means, and I conclude my remarks here. Thank you. Presiding Officer: Honorable Chairperson Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal. (3:34 PM) Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, I will now inform the assembly of the main activities carried out by the National Assembly during the current 29th session. Honorable members, the first meeting of the 21st session of the Federal Parliament, National Assembly, commenced on Monday, Baishakh 28, 2083 BS, at 2:00 PM and continued for a total of 145 days until Friday, Ashoj 16, 2083 BS. During this period, 52 meetings were held, with a total of 98 hours and 10 minutes spent on assembly business. During this session, there was a zero hour in 40 meetings. In that zero hour, 45 honorable members utilized 45 hours and 56 minutes, while there was a special time in 17 meetings. In the special time, 47 honorable members utilized 21 hours and 10 minutes. During this session, there was a provincial concern time in 4 meetings. In the provincial concern time, 27 honorable members utilized 5 hours and 27 minutes, while there was an emergency time in 9 meetings. In the emergency time, 22 honorable members utilized 1 hour and 56 minutes. Honorable members, during this session, the Public Procurement Second Amendment Ordinance, 2083, the Ordinance Relating to Special Arrangements for Public Office Holders, 2083, the Constitutional Council (Work, Duties, Authority, and Procedures) First Amendment Ordinance, 2083, the Anti-Money Laundering Third Amendment Ordinance, 2083, and the Ordinance to Amend Some Nepal Laws, 2083, the Cooperative First Amendment Ordinance, 2083, the Ordinance to Amend Some Nepal Laws Related to Health Sciences Institutes, 2083, and the Ordinance to Amend Some Nepal Laws Related to Universities, 2083, were presented in the assembly. Among these ordinances, the Public Procurement Second Amendment Ordinance, 2083, the Anti-Money Laundering Third Amendment Ordinance, 2083, the Cooperative First Amendment Ordinance, 2083, and the Ordinance to Amend Some Nepal Laws Related to Health Sciences Institutes, 2083, submitted by the government for approval, were approved by the assembly. During this session, the National Assembly passed the Bill on Intangible Cultural Heritage Conservation, 2081, the Infectious Animal Disease (Control) Bill, 2083, and the Bill Relating to the Liability of Domestic Airlines, 2083, and sent them to the House of Representatives with a message. The Bill on the Establishment and Operation of the National Forensic Science Laboratory, 2081, which was returned from the House of Representatives with amendments, was agreed upon by the assembly. During this session, six bills replacing ordinances were sequentially passed by the assembly and sent back to the House of Representatives: the Election to the House of Representatives Member (First Amendment) Bill, 2083, the Voter Roll (First Amendment) Bill, 2083, the Public Procurement (Second Amendment) Bill, 2083, the Anti-Money Laundering (Third Amendment) Bill, 2083, the Cooperative (First Amendment) Bill, 2083, and the Bill to Amend Some Nepal Laws Related to Health Sciences Institutes, 2083. These have also been authenticated. Furthermore, the Appropriation Bill, 2083, the Finance Bill, 2083, and the Bill to Raise National Debt, 2083, received from the House of Representatives with a message, have been passed by both houses and authenticated. During this session, the Bill on Alternative Development Finance Mobilization, 2082, received from the House of Representatives with a message, was tabled in the assembly. This bill has been authenticated during this session. Honorable members, during this session, the Government of Nepal and the concerned ministries were issued rule of law appeals on three matters. The concerned ministers of the Government of Nepal were directed to respond in the National Assembly meeting to the issues raised by the honorable members during the emergency time, zero hour, special time, and provincial concern time. In the National Assembly meeting, regarding the problem faced by the public due to the gas shortage in the market and public grievances raised by honorable members during zero hour and special time, the government's attention was drawn to making necessary arrangements for the smooth supply and sale distribution of gas. Regarding the forecast of heavy to very heavy rainfall in various parts of the country from Ashoj 9 to 11, 2083 BS, with moderate rainfall with thunderstorms in most places, and the high risk of natural disasters such as floods, landslides, and inundation due to heavy rainfall causing huge loss of life and property, everyone was appealed to exercise high vigilance, obtain official and updated information, avoid unnecessary travel, not stay in risky areas, and remain safe. Furthermore, all concerned were directed to keep government mechanisms such as the army, police, and local levels active and in a state of preparedness for risk reduction and response, to create an environment for working in partnership by coordinating with civil society, non-governmental organizations, and local communities, and to increase public awareness by informing citizens about potential risks and their impacts. Honorable members, the President addressed a joint meeting of both houses of the Federal Parliament on Monday, Baishakh 28, 2083 BS. The assembly unanimously passed a motion of thanks for the address. In the joint meeting of the Federal Parliament on Jestha 15, 2083 BS, the annual estimate of revenue and expenditure for the fiscal year 2083/084 was presented. During this period, the assembly discussed the principles and priorities of the Appropriation Bill for the fiscal year 2083/084, excluding tax proposals, and the annual estimate of revenue and expenditure for the fiscal year 2083/084. Furthermore, the policy and program of the Government of Nepal for the fiscal year 2083/084 were discussed and passed by the assembly. Honorable members, during the question-and-answer program held during this session, 35 oral questions related to the Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers, the Ministry of Finance, the Ministry of Health and Population, the Ministry of Agriculture and Forests, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Ministry of Culture, Tourism and Civil Aviation, the Ministry of Physical Infrastructure and Transport, the Ministry of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation, the Ministry of Education, Science and Technology, the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies, the Ministry of Youth, Labour and Employment, the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, and the Ministry of Women, Children, Senior Citizens and Social Security were presented in the assembly. Three written questions related to the Ministry of Culture, Tourism and Civil Aviation were tabled by the concerned minister. Additionally, answers to seven oral questions and one written question related to the Ministry of Finance, the Ministry of Home Affairs, and the Ministry of Physical Infrastructure and Transport, which could not be presented in the assembly, were tabled in the assembly. During this session, Honorable Minister of Foreign Affairs Shishir Khanal and Honorable Minister of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs Sobita Gautam spoke after seeking time on issues raised by honorable members in the assembly during emergency time, zero hour, and special time, as well as on contemporary issues. Honorable members, during the session, a proposal regarding the prevention, control, and protection of women's rights and ensuring access to justice through the use of technology, registered by Honorable Member Renu Chand as the proposer and 18 honorable members as supporters, and a proposal regarding the enactment of laws to regulate the use of assisted reproductive technology, registered by Honorable Member Madan Kumari Shah 'Garima' as the proposer and seven honorable members as supporters, were discussed in the assembly and passed unanimously. Furthermore, instructions were given to implement the proposals with priority. Honorable members, during this session, a proposal to draw the government's attention regarding the preparedness for monsoon-induced disaster management, registered by Honorable Member Kamala Pant as the proposer and four honorable members as supporters, was discussed in the assembly and unanimously approved, and the Ministry of Home Affairs was directed to implement it with priority. Honorable members, during this session, a special proposal was unanimously passed to express heartfelt condolences to the citizens who lost their lives in the tragic incident of loss of life and property due to the devastating flood in the Bhote Koshi River in Rasuwa on Bhadra 10, 2083 BS, and to express deep sympathy to the bereaved families. The proposal also called for coordination among different levels of government, cooperation from local communities, civil society, the private sector, development partners, and the international community for the rescue, relief, rehabilitation of flood victims, search for the missing, free treatment of the injured, scientific management of corpses, and reconstruction of physical infrastructure, to maintain national unity in disaster management, and to adopt effective measures to mitigate disaster risks in the future, with special attention from the Government of Nepal. During this session, Honorable Member Padam Bahadur Pariyar, Honorable Member Madan Kumari Shah 'Garima', Honorable Member Roshni Mechhe, Honorable Member Mohammad Khalid, Honorable Member Tul Prasad Bishwakarma, Honorable Member Krishna Bahadur Rokaya, and Honorable Member Renu Chand were nominated to the Business Advisory Committee. Furthermore, in accordance with Rule 232 'D' of the National Assembly Rules, 2075, to build a common understanding on gender issues and bring such understandings into debate and advocacy, a seven-member Women's Coordination Committee has been formed with the representation of all parties as per the rules, consisting of Honorable Member Durga Gurung, Honorable Member Puja Chaudhary, Honorable Member Meena Singh Rakhal, Honorable Member Rajendra Laxmi Gere, Honorable Member Renu Chand, Honorable Member Vishnu Kumari Sapkota, and Honorable Member Samjhana Devkota. Honorable members, similarly, in accordance with Rule 167 of the National Assembly Rules, 2075...

Following one member, the nine-member Parliamentary Special Committee on the Bhote Koshi and Kaligandaki Corridor Disasters has been formed, including Honourable Member Krishna Prasad Poudel, Honourable Member Gita Devkota, Honourable Member Ghanshyam Rizal, Honourable Member Shrikrishna Prasad Adhikari, Honourable Member Samjhana Devkota, Honourable Member Somnath Pote, Honourable Member Puja Chaudhary, and Honourable Member Tul Prasad Bishwakarma. During this session, the Economic Survey for the fiscal year 2082/083 was presented in the assembly. As per constitutional provisions, annual reports from constitutional bodies were also presented. These reports include the seventh annual report of the National Inclusion Commission for fiscal year 2081/082, the annual report of the Tharu Commission for fiscal year 2081/082, the annual report of the National Dalit Commission for fiscal year 2081/082, the annual report of the Attorney General's Office for fiscal year 2081/082, the annual reports of the Madhesi Commission for fiscal years 2080/081 and 2081/082, the annual report of the National Dalit Commission for fiscal year 2080/089, the annual reports of the National Human Rights Commission for fiscal years 2080/081 and 2081/082, the annual reports of the Judicial Council and the Judicial Service Commission for fiscal years 2080/081 and 2081/082, the annual report of the Public Service Commission for fiscal year 2081/082, the annual report of the National Natural Resources and Fiscal Commission for fiscal year 2081/082, the annual report of the Indigenous Nationalities Commission for fiscal year 2080/081, the 63rd annual report of the Auditor General for 2083, the annual report of the Election Commission for fiscal year 2081/082, and the annual report of the Muslim Commission for fiscal year 2081/082. Furthermore, among the presented reports, the annual report of the National Inclusion Commission for fiscal year 2081/082 was discussed in the assembly, and the government of Nepal was directed to implement the suggestions highlighted in the report. Honourable members, during this session, Honourable Chairperson Krishna Bahadur Rokaya of the Legislation Management Committee presented the committee's report on the bill to revive the previous provisions of the Nepal Special Service Act, 2042, which was sent with a message from the House of Representatives, the committee's report on the Infectious Animal Disease (Control) Bill, 2083, which originated in the National Assembly, the bill concerning the liabilities of domestic air services, 2083, and the annual report of the Legislation Management Committee for fiscal year 2082/083. Honourable Chairperson Krishna Prasad Poudel of the Development, Economic Affairs and Governance Committee presented the study report on drinking water, sanitation, and water resource management in Madhesh Province, 2083, and the annual report of the Development, Economic Affairs and Governance Committee for fiscal year 2082/083. Honourable Chairperson Puja Chaudhary of the Public Policy and Delegated Legislation Committee presented the annual report of the Public Policy and Delegated Legislation Committee for fiscal year 2082/083, and Honourable Chairperson Jayanti Devi Rai of the Federalism Strengthening and National Concerns Committee presented the annual report of the Federalism Strengthening and National Concerns Committee for fiscal year 2082/083. Honourable members, the Government of Nepal has prioritized presenting 166 bills to the federal parliament in the current fiscal year and has submitted them to the Federal Parliament Secretariat. As per the priority of presenting 64 bills in the first four-month period, the federal parliament has presented 24 bills in this current fiscal year, with 22 bills submitted to the House of Representatives and only two bills submitted to the National Assembly. The National Assembly has discussed and passed the government's bills promptly, but it appears that the government has a low priority for submitting bills to the National Assembly. Honourable members, similarly, I addressed the Second Inter-Parliamentary Conference of Speakers held in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, from August 10th to 12th, and during the conference, I held separate bilateral meetings with my counterparts and high-level parliamentary leadership from Cambodia, Australia, Sri Lanka, Pakistan, and the Lao People's Democratic Republic. In my address and bilateral meetings, I seriously raised issues including the significant human and physical damage caused by the devastating flood in the Rasuwa-Bhote Koshi region. In that regard, the Speakers, Chairpersons, and representatives of the parliaments of all participating countries expressed deep sorrow, sympathy, and solidarity regarding the disaster Nepal faced, both in bilateral meetings and during the main session of the conference. Honourable members, during this session, the assembly passed condolence motions on the demise of Rajendra Kharel, former member of the House of Representatives and former minister; Gopal Man Shrestha, former member of the House of Representatives and former Deputy Prime Minister; and Ghanendra Basnet, former member of the House of Representatives. A condolence motion is also on today's agenda to be passed on the demise of Prakash Bahadur Gurung, former member of the House of Representatives and former Assistant Minister. Although this 21st session was the budget session, despite completing the work on time, including the bills received from the government and other businesses, we also experienced the pain of not being able to hold regular meetings due to a lack of business from time to time. Honourable members, I would like to express gratitude on behalf of the assembly to the Honourable Vice-President, all Honourable Members, the thematic committees under the National Assembly, and the Federal Parliament Secretariat for their role in the orderly conduct of the National Assembly's proceedings and the successful completion of some exemplary tasks, as well as the support of the Government of Nepal. I also wish to thank the media for their support in enhancing the effectiveness of the National Assembly and the trust and confidence of civil society and the general public in the assembly. I am confident that the Honourable Members' hard work, the role of the Federal Parliament Secretariat, and the support of the Government of Nepal will be crucial in enhancing the dignity of the assembly in the coming days. Honourable members, on the occasion of the upcoming festivals in Nepal such as Dashain, Tihar, Chhath, Nepal Sambat, Eid, and all cultural festivals of all ethnic groups, I extend my heartfelt best wishes for good health, long life, and continued prosperity to all Nepali sisters and brothers residing in the country and abroad. I look forward to a pleasant reunion in the 22nd session soon. Honourable members, a letter regarding the conclusion of the current 21st session from the Right Honourable President has been received. I will now inform you of the contents of that letter. Honourable President, National Assembly, Singhdarbar, Kathmandu. In accordance with Article 93, Sub-section (2) of the Constitution of Nepal, on the recommendation of the Council of Ministers of the Government of Nepal dated Ashoj 13, 2083, I have concluded the current session of both houses of the Federal Parliament, effective from Friday, Ashoj 16, 2083, at 12:00 AM. Ram Chandra Poudel, President, Ashoj 14, 2083. Honourable members, I now present the condolence motion on the demise of Prakash Bahadur Gurung, former member of the House of Representatives and former Assistant Minister. The National Assembly expresses deep sorrow on the demise of Prakash Bahadur Gurung, former member of the House of Representatives and former Assistant Minister, at the age of 72 on Ashoj 13, 2083. The late Gurung was elected as a member of the House of Representatives from Kaski District Constituency No. 3 in the general elections of 2056 BS from the Nepali Congress party and served as the Assistant Minister of the Ministry of Industry, Commerce, and Supplies during that term. This assembly expresses heartfelt tribute to the late Gurung and deep condolences to his bereaved family. Honourable members, I request that the aforementioned condolence motion be passed unanimously. Honourable members, I declare the aforementioned condolence motion passed unanimously. Honourable members, let us now stand and observe a minute of silence to express sorrow on the demise of Prakash Bahadur Gurung, former member of the House of Representatives and former Assistant Minister. Begin. (Minute of Silence) Thank you. Honourable members, I declare this meeting adjourned, with the current 21st session of the National Assembly automatically concluding today at 12:00 AM. Adjourned: 16:08 hrs.

sections.summary_en: The speaker raises concerns about employment generation, criticizing the government's lack of initiative beyond startup loans and its failure to fulfill promises made to youth seeking overseas employment. They also highlight the severe shortage of agricultural fertilizer, forcing farmers into difficult situations.

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The speaker criticizes the government's attitude towards the opposition, viewing their role as constructive criticism rather than mere opposition. They also discuss the implications of the two-thirds majority in the House of Representatives, warning against arrogance and emphasizing the need for good governance.

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The speaker points out the significant gap in coordination between the federal, provincial, and local governments, especially during disasters. They also criticize the government's lack of sensitivity and accountability in responding to public issues raised in the house and the controversial arrest of a constitutional body official.

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The speaker discusses the rise in cyberattacks and cyberbullying since the current government took office, noting that many politicians have been affected. They also briefly mention the achievements of the past 35 years in various sectors like development, employment, and health, and touch upon the issue of squatters.

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The speaker concludes by referencing the Federal Civil Service Bill, specifically the 55-30 provision, and questions its fairness in light of the government's perceived view of itself as permanent and treating employees as temporary.
